sources.title: DDI Lifecycle 3.3
sources.issuer: Data Documentation Initiative Alliance
sources.contribution: A lifecycle metadata model for concepts, studies, data collection, questionnaires, variables, classifications, sampling plans and frames, weights, and quantitative and qualitative data. Version 3.3 adds non-survey measurements and classification-management updates; the capture model distinguishes reusable questions from their placement/order in an instrument and supports explicit missing-value response domains.
sources.applicability: Use as a seed for linking construct/concept, instrument version, collection event, variable representation, sampling design, and archive lineage without forcing those facets into one domain ontology.
sources.does_not_establish: Schema presence does not establish construct validity, representativeness, a missingness mechanism, causal identification, or permission to use a measurement as authority. A coded missing value records a state; it does not explain why the response is missing.
sources.access_limitations: Public technical documentation is extensive and modular; this record points to the product/version entry page, with the 3.3 data-capture documentation used to verify the specific question, instrument, and missing-value claims.

sources.standing: research source; task applicability and admission not established

sources.title: Magenta Book: Central Government guidance on evaluation
sources.issuer: HM Treasury and Evaluation Task Force, UK Government
sources.contribution: Joins quantitative and qualitative data collection to evaluation questions. It distinguishes probability and non-probability samples, warns that differential non-response can bias inference, describes question development and cognitive testing, and separates qualitative depth/context from statistical representativeness. It also treats existing administrative data, new collection, triangulation, linkage, and data-quality checks as complementary design choices.
sources.applicability: Use for decision-conditioned acquisition: specify which questions need numerical prevalence, which need explanations/experience, when to reuse existing sources, and what sampling, instrument, timing, comparison, and non-response evidence must travel with an observation.
sources.does_not_establish: This is government evaluation guidance, not a universal causal-identification rule or a validated measurement instrument. A large or quota-balanced sample does not by itself warrant population inference; qualitative saturation does not establish prevalence or causal effect.
sources.access_limitations: Open GOV.UK guidance grounded in UK central-government evaluation practice. Methods remain question-, population-, and context-dependent; adapt rather than treat examples as fixed policy-domain templates.

sources.title: Module for Quality Assurance when using Administrative and Other Data Sources to produce Official Statistics
sources.issuer: United Nations Expert Group on National Quality Assurance Frameworks, Subgroup on Administrative and Other Data Sources / UN Statistics Division
sources.version_or_date: Statistical Commission background document, March 2025; endorsed at the 56th session in March 2025
sources.contribution: Separates statistical, administrative, and other-data sources by production purpose; calls for source selection against user need, legal access basis, provider cooperation, input-data and metadata assessment, acquisition/processing, confidentiality, and user-facing quality reporting. It explicitly flags definition, population-coverage, bias, and production-process differences when administrative or other-purpose data are repurposed.
sources.applicability: Use as a source-intake and revalidation checklist for registers, service records, private-sector traces, remote sensing, and citizen-collected data; preserve source purpose and provider/process lineage, then map local concepts and classifications before combining them.
sources.does_not_establish: The module says it complements rather than replaces a national quality framework and does not cover multiple-source use as a complete integration method. It cannot certify access rights, source neutrality, measurement fitness, or causal validity for a specific PolicyOS claim.
sources.access_limitations: The 40-page PDF is English-only in this session; its accompanying checklist is a separate downloadable artifact. It is directed at official-statistics agencies and its suggested practices may not be feasible in every setting.

sources.title: The Global Statistical Geospatial Framework: Implementation Guide
sources.issuer: UN Expert Group on the Integration of Statistical and Geospatial Information / UN Statistics Division and UN-GGIM
sources.contribution: Defines geocoding as linking a statistical-unit location description to coordinates in a coordinate system; explains georeferencing, consistent aggregation/disaggregation and interoperability, and connects spatially enabled statistics to privacy and disclosure controls.
sources.applicability: Treat place as a versioned observation facet: retain location source, geocoder/match quality, coordinate reference system, boundary/grid vintage, unit-level versus aggregate geography, and disclosure treatment. This supports spatially targeted search and local-scale monitoring while exposing aggregation choices.
sources.does_not_establish: A coordinate or successful match does not prove that a geographic unit is the right exposure, that boundaries are comparable across time, that a local estimate is precise, or that an area-level association applies to individuals. Geospatial integration alone does not establish causal structure.
sources.access_limitations: Open 149-page English implementation guide with country examples; national address infrastructure, boundary standards, and implementation capacity vary. The guide is operational guidance, not a universal guarantee of geocoding accuracy.

sources.title: A guide to inclusive social research practices
sources.issuer: Government Social Research Profession, UK Government
sources.contribution: Treats inclusion as a lifecycle concern spanning design, recruitment/data collection, analysis, and reporting. It recommends mapping seldom-heard groups, checking whether the research question itself excludes people, using suitable mixed or qualitative methods, disaggregating where possible, and co-producing work with community leaders; it cautions that weighting only partly addresses selection bias and that purposive qualitative samples do not support statistical generalization.
sources.applicability: Use to identify whose definitions, experiences, and locally meaningful outcomes are absent from the current evidence plan; treat community participation as a way to discover constructs and barriers, while preserving whose views were engaged, how, and with what limits.
sources.does_not_establish: The guide is high-level advice, not proof that any sample is inclusive, that a community representative speaks for every member, or that participation itself authorizes normative weights or objectives. Group labels and subgroup boundaries remain context-sensitive.
sources.access_limitations: Open UK-government guidance from 2022; intended as a starting point rather than detailed population-specific instructions. Applicability to another jurisdiction requires local review and language/access adaptation.

sources.title: June 2025 Update to Global Poverty Lines
sources.issuer: World Bank
sources.contribution: Sets the international extreme-poverty line at $3.00 per person per day in 2021 PPP dollars, with $4.20 and $8.30 lines for lower- and upper-middle-income contexts. sources.does_not_establish: Does not establish a universal or country-specific eligibility threshold, nor that PPP and line updates reveal a change in people's lived conditions.

sources.title: OECD Guidelines for Citizen Participation Processes
sources.issuer: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD)
sources.contribution: Sets out ten steps and eight participation methods, including open consultation, citizen science, participatory budgeting, and representative deliberative processes. The guidance says to involve citizens only when there is meaningful room for influence, to define expected results and how input affects the final decision, and to evaluate process quality, neutrality, accessibility, integrity, and follow-through. It distinguishes outputs that range from ideas or recommendations to binding resource allocation through a vote in a properly designed participatory budgeting process.
sources.applicability: Design: bind the question, decision stage, participant population, recruitment and selection method, resources, and promised influence. Search: retain participant recommendations as one input and disclose process limits. Learning: preserve experience and knowledge as evidence with its source and date. Observability: show reach, inclusion, response to input, dissent, and whether the authority acted on it.
sources.does_not_establish: A poll or consultation does not establish representativeness, a binding mandate, or legality. The specific process and institutional authority determine whether a given output has decision force.
sources.access_limitations: The official OECD publication page and full English PDF were accessible. This is process guidance, not jurisdiction-specific law or an authorization for a particular public decision.

sources.title: A Difficulty in the Concept of Social Welfare
sources.issuer: Kenneth J. Arrow; Journal of Political Economy, University of Chicago Press
sources.contribution: Arrow's possibility theorem shows that with at least three alternatives and unrestricted individual orderings, a social ordering satisfying the paper's stated rationality and aggregation conditions must be imposed or dictatorial. The paper also makes explicit that the result depends on its assumptions, including ordinal rankings and the exclusion of interpersonal utility comparisons.
sources.applicability: Design: treat a social ranking rule as a value choice with named assumptions and an authorized owner. Search: expose alternative aggregation rules, sensitivity, Pareto trade-offs, and unresolved disagreement instead of presenting a single score as neutral. Learning: preference changes can update inputs to a declared rule, not select the rule itself. Observability: retain the rule version, preference basis, excluded information, and groups whose rankings are absent.
sources.does_not_establish: It does not show that all democratic decision-making is impossible, that no aggregation method is useful, or that one particular social welfare rule is correct. Its conclusion is conditional on the article's formal domain and axioms.
sources.access_limitations: The publisher DOI page is bibliographic and requires subscription for the full article. The original 1950 article scan hosted by the University of Chicago Department of Statistics was accessible and used to check the theorem and assumptions.

verification.method: Read the original paper scan and checked its theorem statement and discussion of aggregation conditions.
verification.evidence: The paper's possibility theorem section states the result for at least three alternatives and distinguishes imposed from dictatorial functions. Its interpretation section explains that excluding interpersonal utility comparisons is material to the result. The scan footer confirms the Journal of Political Economy citation and 1950 publication.

sources.title: Theory of Games and Economic Behavior
sources.issuer: John von Neumann and Oskar Morgenstern; Princeton University Press
sources.version_or_date: First published 1944; publisher digital edition DOI 10.1515/9781400829460
sources.kind: primary formal decision-theory and game-theory monograph
sources.contribution: The book's axiomatic treatment of utility provides a formal representation of preferences over risky prospects under stated assumptions. A von Neumann-Morgenstern utility can encode one decision maker's risk attitude over a specified lottery; it is a representation result, not an empirical claim that all people behave that way.
sources.applicability: Design: specify outcomes, probability basis, actor, and risk preference separately. Search: compare expected utility only under an admitted preference and probability model, then show sensitivity to alternative risk attitudes and tail outcomes. Learning: choices may inform descriptive risk-preference estimates, with context, incentives, and uncertainty retained. Observability: preserve who supplied the risk schedule, when, and for which decisions.
sources.does_not_establish: The formal representation does not determine social welfare weights, whose preferences count, whether observed choices are stable or legitimate, the quality of the probability model, or whether rights may be traded against expected benefit.
sources.access_limitations: The publisher-hosted edition and table of contents are available online. The publisher's table of contents identifies the axiomatic treatment of utility, but full theorem pages were not exposed by the browser extraction in this session.

verification.method: Checked the publisher's digital edition metadata and contents, and the publisher-hosted 60th-anniversary edition front matter and contents.
verification.evidence: The original monograph is dated 1944. Its contents include the axiomatic treatment of numerical utilities, the utility axioms and their interpretation, and the role of marginal utility.

sources.title: The Basic Liberties and Their Priority
sources.issuer: John Rawls; Tanner Lectures on Human Values, University of Utah Press
sources.contribution: Rawls's two principles give equal basic liberties priority over the second principle concerning fair opportunity and the greatest benefit to the least advantaged. In the lecture, basic liberties cannot be denied for aggregate public-good or efficiency gains, though liberties must be regulated into a coherent scheme and the priority argument is conditioned on reasonably favorable social circumstances.
sources.applicability: Design: represent rights floors and priority rules separately from benefit measures where an applicable authority adopts them. Search: eliminate options that violate an admitted rights constraint before comparing distributive outcomes; show any rights conflict explicitly. Learning: outcome gains do not by themselves erase a rights violation. Observability: show the source and scope of each constraint and any remaining interpretive question.
sources.does_not_establish: Rawls presents a contested normative account, not universal law or a universal list of rights. The lecture itself says the priority argument is conditional and leaves further specification to constitutional, legislative, and judicial stages.
sources.access_limitations: The Tanner Lectures archive provides the full text of the 1982 lecture as a PDF and readable page.

verification.method: Read the lecture text and checked its statement of the two principles, the priority rule, and stated limits.
verification.evidence: Sections I and II state the equal-liberty and distributive principles, the priority of the first over the second, the prohibition on trading basic liberties for aggregate gains, the need to reconcile liberties, and the reasonably favorable conditions qualification.

sources.title: Crossref typed relationships and Crossmark update metadata
sources.issuer: Crossref
sources.version_or_date: Current Crossref relationships/Crossmark documentation checked 2026-10-20; REST filter page last updated 2025-10-16
sources.contribution: Crossref documents typed links among works, datasets, and software, including dataset supplements, versions, derivations, and Crossmark update relations. REST filters expose `has-update`, `is-update`, and update types such as correction or retraction. These signals can support report/dataset lineage discovery and post-publication revalidation.
sources.applicability: Resolve research-object relationships and update/retraction notices during discovery, deduplication, freshness checks, and lifecycle reassessment; follow the related notice and original content rather than treating a metadata edge as the full evidence.
sources.does_not_establish: Completeness of a work's relationship graph, methodological independence, truth of the linked claim, or that an item with no Crossmark/update relation has never changed.
sources.access_limitations: Crossmark is member- and publisher-deposited metadata; participation and backfile coverage are not universal. Crossref documentation says metadata is supplied by members, and Crossmark presence is not a guarantee of record completeness.

sources.title: HM Treasury Magenta Book, Annex A: analytical methods for evaluation
sources.issuer: HM Treasury and Evaluation Task Force, United Kingdom
sources.contribution: Maps evaluation questions to theory-based, experimental/quasi-experimental, value-for-money, and evidence-synthesis methods. It describes process tracing, realist evaluation, and qualitative comparative analysis for mechanisms/context and notes that theory-based methods may explain attribution without precise effect sizes. It presents systematic review and meta-analysis strengths alongside resource, evidence-volume, and bias limitations.
sources.applicability: Policy-domain anchor for triangulating causal mechanisms, implementation/context, and quantitative effect evidence; use method-purpose fit and preserve each method's warrant and limitations.
sources.does_not_establish: That triangulation automatically creates independent confirmation, that every method estimates an average causal effect, or that UK evaluation guidance is binding across jurisdictions or domains.
sources.access_limitations: Official HM Treasury HTML guidance opened. It is government evaluation guidance rather than a universal synthesis standard; some methods depend on expert judgment and may be resource-intensive or context-specific.

sources.title: The FAIR Guiding Principles for scientific data management and stewardship
sources.issuer: Wilkinson et al., Scientific Data (Nature Portfolio)
sources.contribution: Sets out machine- and human-oriented findability, accessibility, interoperability, and reusability principles; accessibility permits authentication and authorization where needed.
sources.applicability: Use persistent identification, searchable metadata, shared vocabularies, explicit access procedures, provenance, and reuse conditions as design prompts for source handling.
sources.does_not_establish: That a resource must be open, is true or high quality, is admissible for a particular claim, is legally reusable by PolicyOS, or is independent of another source. Those conclusions require separate evidence and scope.
sources.access_limitations: Principles paper, not a specific runtime protocol or universal conformance test; reuse and access decisions remain context-dependent.
sources.verification: Checked the DOI publication record and the original paper record; the article presents FAIR as guiding principles and includes authentication/authorization for controlled access where necessary.
sources.standing: research source; task applicability and admission not established

additional_research_uses.contribution: Defines guidance for improving Findability, Accessibility, Interoperability, and Reusability of research data and metadata.
additional_research_uses.applicability: Use FAIR practices to make eligible source material discoverable, interpretable, and reproducible; decide rights, consent, ethics, and allowed use separately for each asset and purpose.
additional_research_uses.does_not_establish: That data are open, lawfully obtained, ethically reusable, accurate, independent, or licensed for PolicyOS processing. This is a scope limitation inferred from the article’s data-management purpose, not a FAIR rights grant.

sources.title: Verifiable Credentials Data Model v2.0
sources.issuer: World Wide Web Consortium (W3C), Verifiable Credentials Working Group
sources.contribution: Describes issuer, claims, proofs, validity dates, credential status, and verification. It explicitly distinguishes credential authenticity/currentness from claim truth and says issuer trust decisions are verifier-specific and out of scope.
sources.applicability: Useful reference when an external source issues signed rights, consent, or status evidence; verify issuer, proof, subject, currency/status, and claims for the particular purpose. The spec also warns about correlation and privacy leakage from persistent identifiers and status checks.
sources.does_not_establish: Truth or legal effect of claims, that a particular issuer is trusted for a particular purpose, or that every source uses a VC-compatible proof.
sources.access_limitations: The recommendation defines a data model and ecosystem, not a universal trust list or a domain-specific claim-validation policy.
sources.verification: Opened W3C Recommendation dated 2025-05-15; §1.1 distinguishes verifiability from claim truth, §5.1 places issuer-trust decisions outside the model, and §8 Privacy Considerations discusses correlation and status-check leakage.
